A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GOAL research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on eight training tasks, transfer to eight further tasks, architectural ablations and size generalization.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds baseline comparisons, further size-generalization results and a frozen-backbone control.

M1.justification: The shared backbone, adapters, codebook, mixed attention, multi-type architecture and training objectives remain unchanged. Section 3.6 and Appendix D explain the existing procedure; backbone freezing is added as an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight training problems and eight transfer problems. The expanded generalization experiments evaluate larger instances of retained problems, without introducing new task requirements or dataset families.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RouteFinder-TE for CVRP and CVRPTW and Gumbeldore for JSSP. Table 2 adds explicit traditional-solver comparison rows, while retaining the neural comparators in its existing ATSP and CVRP comparisons.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include frozen-backbone fine-tuning, HGS one-second versus one-minute budgets, and additional size grids, including JSSP 10x15, 15x15 and 20x15. The core training budget, architecture sizes and existing evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a control testing whether updating the pretrained backbone matters during supervised transfer. Table 2 substantially broadens size-generalization analysis from ATSP and CVRP to include CVRPTW, OP, KP and JSSP. The existing attention, multi-type and codebook ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report best-of-ten fine-tuning results and retain the same ten-run codebook analysis and confidence-interval description. No new seed reporting, uncertainty estimation procedure or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: Numerous reported scores and timings change. In Table 1, multi-task ATSP rises from 0.50% to 0.91% and UMSP from 2.01% to 3.84%; Table 2's ATSP1000 gap changes from 2.37% to 1.96%, with runtime changing from 28 to 5 minutes. v3 also adds extensive scaling results and frozen-backbone curves. The PDFs do not explain the numerical revisions.

T1.justification: The tail-recursive multi-task formulation and mixed-attention equations remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of bisimulation, low-rank projections and type combinations do not introduce new proofs or substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: a generalist backbone across CO domains, efficient transfer to new problems and strong single-task performance on seven of eight training tasks.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies Table 1's gaps as relative to the oracle, rather than necessarily the optimum. Section 4.3 additionally discusses relaxing parameter sharing between type-specific attention blocks during fine-tuning. The existing feasibility and quadratic-scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds the 2.1-million-parameter backbone size, approximate adapter sizes and clearer node/edge dimensions. Appendix D and Figure 8 explain scheduling-specific inputs and attention blocks. Existing hardware, optimizer settings and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on random-feature GNNs, bandit-based multi-task training and MCTS, replaces the Bertsekas book reference and removes the t-SNE reference. The broad positioning against specialized and routing-focused models remains unchanged; many other reference edits concern bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The title expansion changes from Agent Learning to Agent Learner. v3 adds a dedicated training-procedure subsection and scheduling appendix, and refines explanations of BQ-MDPs, adapters and problem definitions. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2's multi-type schematic is substantially redrawn, Figure 8 adds scheduling diagrams, and Figure 6 gains a third series and shared legend. Table 2 is substantially expanded and reorganized, and Table 1 is resized with additional rows. Earlier Figures 3–5 are retained with changed numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: Additional comparators, broader size-generalization evidence and the frozen-backbone control strengthen validation, while architectural disclosures improve clarity. These are useful, bounded gains over v2's existing empirical case. Unexplained numerical revisions and the conflict between Section 4's all-greedy statement and Table 2's COMPASS exception limit the improvement.
